target_customer: Medical residency programs and hospital graduate medical education administrators
problem: Residency scheduling is a large logistics burden for hospitals. ReSchedule Med offered an end to end workflow to build and manage residency schedules.

founders.name: Taylor Fairbank
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only active founder, an open source maintainer and later co-founder of Distribute Aid in 2019.

exit.reason: YC lists the company as inactive. No shutdown announcement or acquisition was found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling workflows with duty hour and rotation rules are standard business software for a small team, with some constraint logic.

defensibility.rationale: Once programs adopt a scheduler it is sticky, but the product was early and incumbent residency management vendors could add scheduling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent residency vendors exist today and QGenda bought New Innovations in 2025. No source shows any of them acting against ReSchedule Med.

market_need_then: The company's own pitch states that scheduling is one of the largest logistics pain points in hospitals and residency programs. No dated external evidence was found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand material was found.

outcome_analysis: ReSchedule Med was a one founder New York company in YC W15 targeting residency program scheduling. It is marked inactive, but no shutdown announcement, post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause of failure is not public and no failure factors are assigned. The only funding figure is a 120 thousand dollar seed from one database.
notes: Company website returned an HTTP 520 error, so it is treated as unreachable. The 120K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, via search summary). Searches for dated 2015 competitors found only current vendor pages, so the list is empty by rule. The incumbent names MedHub, New Innovations and Amion appear in takeover_risk_then from current pages and are not asserted as competitors as of founding. Cause of inactivity not public.
